source: ACIAR Monograph No. 146a, "ដំណាំសំណែកសៀង" [Soybean Growers Manual], Belfield S., Brown C., Martin M. (eds.), New South Wales Department of Primary Industries / Murdoch University / CARDI / ACIAR, 2012
text: Land preparation: covers both animal-drawn plough/harrow and tractor-drawn implements, aiming for a fine, weed-free, well-drained seedbed. The manual gives guidance on machinery-based row seeding versus manual dibbling, with row spacing and in-row plant spacing recommendations, and recommends planting into residual soil moisture at the start of the wet season or with irrigation for dry-season crops. A photo shows a tractor-drawn multi-row precision seeder used for larger-scale Cambodian soybean planting alongside more traditional hand-planting.
